End-to-end workflow: from CDS to crop model

ag5_workflow.Rmd

Overview

This article walks through the complete ag5Tools workflow:

  1. Download AgERA5 .nc files from the Copernicus Climate Data Store.
  2. Extract time series of specific variables for field trial locations.
  3. Prepare APSIM meteorological files for crop simulation.

The example uses the arusha_df dataset bundled with the package — 100 synthetic field trial plots in the Arusha region, Tanzania, each with planting and harvest dates.

library(ag5Tools)

data("arusha_df", package = "ag5Tools")
head(arusha_df)
#>        lon       lat start_date   end_date
#> 1 35.72636 -2.197162 1991-04-22 1991-08-20
#> 2 36.10249 -2.850983 1990-01-24 1990-05-24
#> 3 35.46292 -3.602582 1991-03-06 1991-07-04
#> 4 36.29166 -3.855945 1990-10-10 1991-02-07
#> 5 35.45254 -3.616361 1990-01-22 1990-05-22
#> 6 35.40131 -3.216106 1990-10-19 1991-02-16

The four columns are: lon, lat (decimal degrees, WGS84), start_date, end_date (YYYY-MM-DD character strings). These match the default argument names in ag5_extract().

Step 1: Download AgERA5 data

Before extracting, the corresponding AgERA5 files must be on disk. Downloads are organised by variable and year; downloading a full year of daily global data for one variable takes a few minutes depending on connection speed.

The area argument limits the download to the bounding box of interest. Here we use a rough bounding box covering the Arusha region.

# Date range covered by arusha_df
range(as.Date(arusha_df$start_date))
range(as.Date(arusha_df$end_date))

# Download precipitation for the relevant period
ag5_download(
  variable = "precipitation_flux",
  year     = 2015,
  month    = "all",
  day      = "all",
  area     = c(-2, 35, -4, 38),   # c(north, west, south, east)
  path     = "C:/agera5_data"
)

# Download daily maximum temperature
ag5_download(
  variable  = "2m_temperature",
  statistic = "24_hour_maximum",
  year      = 2015,
  month     = "all",
  day       = "all",
  area      = c(-2, 35, -4, 38),
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

# Download solar radiation
ag5_download(
  variable = "solar_radiation_flux",
  year     = 2015,
  month    = "all",
  day      = "all",
  area     = c(-2, 35, -4, 38),
  path     = "C:/agera5_data"
)

Step 2: Extract data for field trial locations

ag5_extract() accepts a data.frame as coords. Each row defines a location and date range; the function returns a list of named numeric vectors — one per row.

Precipitation time series 

rainfall <- ag5_extract(
  coords   = arusha_df,
  variable = "Precipitation-Flux",
  path     = "C:/agera5_data"
)

# Each element is a named numeric vector covering that plot's date range
length(rainfall)      # 100
length(rainfall[[1]]) # number of days between start_date and end_date for plot 1
head(rainfall[[1]])

Maximum temperature time series 

maxt <- ag5_extract(
  coords    = arusha_df,
  variable  = "Temperature-Air-2m",
  statistic = "Max-24h",
  celsius   = TRUE,
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

Single-point, single-date extraction

For a quick check, coords can be a numeric vector and dates a single date string.

ag5_extract(
  coords    = c(lon = 36.68, lat = -3.37),
  dates     = "2015-06-15",
  variable  = "Temperature-Air-2m",
  statistic = "Max-24h",
  celsius   = TRUE,
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

Column name flexibility

If your data.frame uses different column names, pass them explicitly.

my_trials <- data.frame(
  x         = arusha_df$lon,
  y         = arusha_df$lat,
  planting  = arusha_df$start_date,
  harvest   = arusha_df$end_date
)

rain2 <- ag5_extract(
  coords     = my_trials,
  lon        = "x",
  lat        = "y",
  start_date = "planting",
  end_date   = "harvest",
  variable   = "Precipitation-Flux",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data"
)

Parallel extraction for large datasets

For large data.frame inputs, enable parallel processing to speed things up.

rainfall_par <- ag5_extract(
  coords   = arusha_df,
  variable = "Precipitation-Flux",
  path     = "C:/agera5_data",
  parallel = TRUE,
  ncores   = 4
)

Step 3: Summarise extracted data

Once extracted, the list of time series can be summarised into trial-level statistics for analysis or modelling.

# Total rainfall over each trial's growing season
total_rain <- sapply(rainfall, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
summary(total_rain)

# Days with rainfall > 1 mm
rainy_days <- sapply(rainfall, function(x) sum(x > 1, na.rm = TRUE))
summary(rainy_days)

Step 4: Prepare APSIM meteorological files

For crop simulation with APSIM, use ag5_apsim(). It extracts all required variables for a single location, applies unit conversions, computes site constants, and writes a .met file in one call.

Classic APSIM .met file 

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2010-01-01",
  end_date   = "2020-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha",
  format     = "classic"
)

APSIM Next Generation output 

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2010-01-01",
  end_date   = "2020-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha",
  format     = "apsimng"
)

Download missing files on the fly

If AgERA5 files are missing for any date in the requested range, download = TRUE fetches them automatically before extracting.

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015",
  download   = TRUE
)

Inspect site constants without writing a file

Leave filename = NULL to get the data.frame back with tav and amp as attributes.

met <- ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  variables  = "required",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data"
)
#> Site constants:
#>   latitude  = -3.37 (degrees)
#>   longitude = 36.68 (degrees)
#>   tav = 20.34 (oC)
#>   amp = 1.72 (oC)

attr(met, "tav")
attr(met, "amp")

Note on variable naming

ag5_download() uses CDS API variable names (snake_case: "2m_temperature", "24_hour_maximum", "06_00"). ag5_extract() uses the file names written to disk by the CDS (Title-Case-hyphen: "Temperature-Air-2m", "Max-24h", "06h"). These are two different naming systems reflecting the upstream API and file formats — they are not errors.

ag5_apsim() handles this translation internally; you do not need to manage the naming difference when using it.
